newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian govt, PM opinion poll lead dips.
newsitem.headline: Australian govt, PM opinion poll lead dips.

text.p: The conservative Australian government's poll lead over the Labor opposition has dipped, amid rows over ministerial business interests and the prime minister's overseas trip, a newspaper poll said on Tuesday.

Support for Prime Minister John Howard's Liberal-National coalition fell two points to 42 percent over the past two weeks, with the government's lead over Labor dropping to five points from eight, the Australian national daily's Newspoll found.
Labor's support rose one point to 37 percent.

Support for far right populist Pauline Hanson's One Nation Party fell one point to six percent, well down from its high of nine percent in early and mid-May, but equal to the traditional third political bloc, the Australian Democrats.
Democrats support rose to six percent from three.

The Australian's latest measure of primary support compares with the government's primary vote of 47.3 percent and Labor's 38.8 percent in the March 1996 election, that saw Howard sweep into office and end 13 years of Labor rule.
Howard's lead over opposition leader Kim Beazley as preferred prime minister has also fallen.
Howard's rating fell five points to 42 percent, as Beazley's rose five points to 30 percent. But 28 percent of those surveyed were uncommitted.
The poll surveyed 1,152 voters around the country by telephone over the weekend of June 27-29.
